html:
A Vietnamese scholar, strategist and poet who was the chief adviser of Lê Lợi in the war that freed Vietnam from Ming rule. He wrote its most famous text, the Great Proclamation of 1428.

Nguyễn Trãi passed the court exams in 1400 under the short lived Hồ dynasty. When the Ming conquered the country in 1407, his father was taken prisoner to China. Nguyễn Trãi joined Lê Lợi's Lam Sơn uprising, which began in 1418. He wrote the letters that urged Ming garrisons to surrender and the appeals that won over the people. When the Ming withdrew in 1427, he wrote the Bình Ngô đại cáo, which declared that Đại Việt had its own land, customs and rulers, equal to China's.

He served the new Lê court but fell out of favour. In 1442 the young king Lê Thái Tông died suddenly after visiting his estate, and Nguyễn Trãi and three generations of his family were executed. King Lê Thánh Tông cleared his name in 1464. His poems in chữ Nôm, the Vietnamese script, are among the earliest great works in the language of Đại Việt.
sum: A Vietnamese scholar, strategist and poet who was the chief adviser of Lê Lợi in the war that freed Vietnam from Ming rule. He wrote its most famous text, the Great Proclamation of 1428.
